contradicting_evidence: Stablecoin supply contraction across daily, weekly and monthly windows, together with negative latest settled ETF flows, supports a tentative downside case.
The broad rebound and strong 24h ETH performance support a competing repair or expansion case.
The 30d altseason measure remains in Bitcoin Season, which argues against assuming that an absolute rebound will develop into sustained altcoin outperformance.
frozen_forecast.expected_path: No supported net weekly direction can be assigned. A durable recovery would require repeated confirmation from prices, relative leadership, participation and demand; renewed contraction would require evidence that the rebound is failing. The supplied snapshots do not establish which path will dominate over seven days.
falsification_conditions: A persistent sequence of price resilience, stronger ETH/BTC, broader relative participation and improved settled flows would establish a more credible upside case.
A persistent sequence of failed rebounds, deteriorating breadth, ETH-relative weakness and continued negative settled flows would establish a more credible downside case.
missing_evidence: No current multi-day price, volume or participation sequence establishes the durability of the rebound.
Repeated subsequent settled ETF sessions and an updated stablecoin supply trajectory are unavailable.
No observed deployment evidence connects available stablecoin supply to sustained risk-asset demand.
A supported forward catalyst schedule and comprehensive cross-capitalization coverage, especially below the Top-100, are unavailable.
supporting_evidence: The daily rebound is constructive, while negative settled flows and contracting stablecoin supply challenge its durability; neither side establishes a weekly trend.
Longer participation windows are inconsistent with a simple expansion narrative: the 30d altseason score is 20, while the supplied 90d scores are 41 and 48.
Current capitalization proxies demonstrate absolute participation but not broad relative leadership, and cannot establish a full-market rotation.
The structural prior describes unresolved repair and retest possibilities, but supplies no independently confirmed forward transition.
